metais inspect — Print what a supplier reads first: the package's identity, its
guide, its inputs, outputs, references and examples, and the commands to run
next.

Usage:
  metais inspect <package> [--guide] [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

Examples:
  metais inspect report-1.0.0.metais
      Prints the summary of a packed package.
  metais inspect .
      Prints the summary of the source directory in the working directory.
  metais inspect report-1.0.0.metais --guide
      Prints the package's whole guide.
  metais inspect report-1.0.0.metais --json
      Prints the summary as one metais.inspect/1 document.

The package is a packed package file or a source directory. Before it prints
anything, inspect verifies the whole package: every entry's name and data, the
digest of every entry and of the package, the manifest under the specification
version it declares, every schema, and each compiled file against the sources it
is derived from. A package that fails any check is refused with every finding of
the check, and nothing of it is printed.

The digest of a source directory is the digest of the package metais pack would
write from it, computed in memory; nothing is written.

A guide of more than 60 lines or 6144 bytes is cut to its first 40 lines, within
4096 bytes; --guide prints it whole, and nothing else.

The Next: block lists the commands that fill in and render the package, then
metais render --sample and metais sample, which serve a supplier who wants an
example, a preview or data to start from with data generated from the inputs'
schemas, then the first of the package's examples, and last the way to edit the
package: metais unpack for a packed package, metais check for a source
directory. An example is the author's illustration of the inputs, and of the
outputs a render of them should produce, kept in the package to test it: not
your data.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.

Flags:
  --guide
      Print only the whole guide: its Markdown alone, or with --json the
      package's identity and the guide.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  The package's summary: its title, name and version, description, specification
  version, form and digest, then the sections Guide, Inputs, Outputs,
  References, Assets and Examples, then the Next: block; with --guide, the
  guide's Markdown alone. With --json, one metais.inspect/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais inspect --help
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais inspect --help
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais inspect --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais inspect --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais inspect --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais inspect --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals inspect' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  manifest.* (44)  The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (47)   The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)    An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  template.* (9)   An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
